# Warrior One Adjustment

Great effort! I can see you're really engaging with this pose. Let me help you refine your alignment so you can get the most out of Warrior One. I've noticed a few things we can work on together:

**Your Spine:** Right now, your spine isn't quite straight—I can see a slight curve or lean. This is a common adjustment! To fix this, imagine a string pulling the top of your head toward the sky. Lengthen through your entire spine and draw your shoulders back slightly. This will help you maintain that beautiful, upright posture that protects your back and lets the pose work for you.

**Your Arms:** Your arms aren't quite reaching their full potential yet. They're getting there, but I'd like to see them fully extended overhead. Really press through your palms and reach your fingers up toward the ceiling. Keep your shoulders relaxed away from your ears as you do this. This extension will help you experience the full stretch and strength-building benefits of the pose.

**Your Front Knee:** Excellent that you're thinking about your foundation! Make sure your front knee is stacking directly over your ankle. You might need to adjust your stance slightly—bring your back foot in a bit more if needed. This alignment protects your knee and gives you a more stable base for the pose.

You're doing wonderful work, and these refinements are going to take your practice to the next level! Ready to give it another try?
